newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Timor car targets 40 pct market share.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Timor car targets 40 pct market share.

text.p: The makers of Indonesia's so-called national car have said they hope to eventually control 40 percent of the domestic market, the official Antara news agency said on Sunday.

"Our market share will be no more than 40 percent," said Hutomo Mandala Putra whose joint venture company PT Timor Putra Nasional was given special tax and tariff breaks in February to produce sedans under the government's national car policy.
Mandala Putra said his company, a joint venture with Kia Motors of South Korea, would only produce around 200,000 cars a year. He said current annual domestic demand for cars was at around 400,000.
"Opportunities are still open for other car manufacturers as demand will continue to rise," Mandala Putra, President Suharto's youngest son, was quoted as saying.

PT Timor Putra Nasional is currently importing fully made up cars from Korea ahead of its Timor sedan entering the market next month. It plans to open an assembly plant in West Java in March next year.
The company must meet local content requirements of 20 percent in the first year and 60 percent by the end of the third year to qualify for its luxury tax and tariff exemptions.
Under its national car policy the government has given the tax breaks only to PT Timor Putra Nasional. It has said the policy is designed to promote a local automotive component industry.
